first_impression: Nice vintage editorial look, but it starts too slowly and feels more like a templated history explainer than a sharp food-brand post.
problems: The cover is not publication-ready because the giant year appears mid-transition as a weird, unreadable number.
Too much time is spent on the 1893 setup with almost no new information in the first four seconds.
The pacing is slow for Shorts/Reels; several frames reveal one word at a time without enough payoff.
The food image looks like modern pasta with tomatoes, not tomatoes/imports/Supreme Court, so it feels like stock filler.
The story logic is slightly muddy: it says the Court agreed tomatoes are fruit, then jumps to vegetable without clearly explaining common-use classification fast enough.
Small source text at the bottom is hard to read and may be covered by platform UI.
The final brand tie-in in the caption is not visually earned in the video and makes the post feel like a disguised ad.
The layout repeats the same beige background, red highlight blocks, and centered text rhythm for too long.
fixes: Export a clean cover frame with the full year ‘1893’ visible, not a transition frame.
Make the first frame a stronger hook: ‘The Supreme Court once ruled a tomato was a vegetable’ or ‘A tomato went to the Supreme Court over taxes.’
Cut the opening hold to under 1 second and get to the tariff conflict immediately.
Use more relevant imagery: tomatoes in crates, an old customs document, a court engraving, or a simple illustrated tomato with tax labels instead of generic pasta.
Condense the narrative to 10–14 seconds: hook, 10% vegetable tariff, fruit was free, importer sued, Court said botanical fruit but legal vegetable.
Replace word-by-word captions with full short lines so viewers can read faster.
Move or enlarge the source citation so it is legible and not in the platform-button danger zone.
Add a sharper final beat on-screen, e.g. ‘Botany lost. Taxes won.’ instead of relying on the caption for payoff.
If promoting RecipeFix, make the CTA subtler and food-native, or put it only in the profile/comment rather than the main caption.
